title: VP of Operations

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: Managing 400,000+ square feet of manufacturing and converting operations across multiple geographies, the VP of Operations at General Formulations would be critical for scaling Tedlar adoption across additional product SKUs beyond GF 108. This role would care about: (1) operational efficiency and yield optimization—converting and laminating Tedlar film requires specific technical expertise; expanding usage across more product lines would benefit from standardized processes and supplier consolidation with an existing trusted partner, (2) quality metrics and warranty claim reduction—if non-Tedlar laminates are generating field failures, defects, or customer returns, upgrading to Tedlar's proven durability (no yellowing, UV degradation, graffiti resistance) directly improves operational KPIs and reduces costly rework, (3) supply chain reliability and inventory management—deepening the existing Tedlar partnership provides supplier stability and potentially better pricing/terms for higher volume commitments across multiple SKUs, (4) capacity utilization—with established converting capabilities, adding Tedlar-backed premium SKUs allows GF to drive higher revenue per square foot of manufacturing capacity without major capex investment. Given that GF already successfully manufactures GF 108 Tedlar laminate, Operations has proven competency to scale Tedlar into wall protection, architectural graphics, and transit interior applications where the company currently serves customers but may be using less durable alternatives.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: [Name] oversees 400,000+ square feet of manufacturing and converting operations across General Formulations' global footprint (US, Canada, LATAM, APAC, Europe). They own operational efficiency, quality metrics, supply chain stability, and manufacturing capacity utilization. With 116 employees supporting $63.9M in revenue, this role likely reports directly to the CEO/President and has direct authority over production planning, procurement decisions, and manufacturing process standardization. Given GF's existing Tedlar partnership for GF 108, [Name] already has experience with Tedlar converting operations and would influence decisions about expanding Tedlar usage across additional product lines beyond the current anti-graffiti laminate.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: General Formulations currently manufactures GF 108 with Tedlar for anti-graffiti applications. Relevant expansion opportunities for [Name]'s operations include: (1) Wall protection/covering products—GF serves this vertical but may use non-Tedlar alternatives that generate warranty claims or quality issues; (2) Architectural graphics and building wraps—GF has demonstrated capability in outdoor applications (120+ LA Metro buses wrapped) but could standardize on Tedlar for all architectural SKUs to reduce SKU complexity and supplier count; (3) Transit and rail interiors—existing MetroMark 209 transit product line could be upgraded or expanded with Tedlar-backed variants for interior applications requiring graffiti resistance and cleaning chemical tolerance; (4) Premium vehicle wrap overlaminates—GF partners with PDAA for fleet training using GF 830 AutoMark Cast, representing an opportunity to differentiate premium fleet products with Tedlar protection. Each use case allows [Name] to leverage existing converting expertise while improving yield, reducing defects, and driving higher revenue per manufacturing square foot.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: [Name] is likely measured on: manufacturing yield and waste reduction, on-time delivery and production efficiency, warranty claim rates and quality defects, supply chain cost and supplier performance, and capacity utilization metrics. Expanding Tedlar adoption directly impacts these KPIs by: reducing rework and scrap from failed laminates that don't meet durability specs, decreasing warranty exposure from premature UV degradation or graffiti damage in the field, consolidating supplier relationships to improve purchasing leverage and reduce inventory complexity, and enabling premium-priced SKUs that generate higher margin per square foot of manufacturing capacity without major capex investment. [Name] has already proven operational competency with Tedlar through GF 108 success, so scaling to additional products represents lower implementation risk compared to onboarding a new material supplier.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: General Formulations co-exhibited with DuPont Tedlar at ISA Expo 2025 in April with joint anti-graffiti product demonstrations and booth challenges between the two companies. This recent joint marketing activity signals an active, strategic partnership at the executive level. Additionally, GF showcased new Economy Film & Laminate Solutions at ISA 2025 and launched GF 767 Sparkle Holographic Film at PRINTING United Expo 2024, indicating active product portfolio expansion. With upcoming PRINTING United Expo 2025 where GF will exhibit again, [Name] is likely evaluating manufacturing capacity allocation and product mix decisions for the next 6-12 months. The timing is ideal to discuss scaling Tedlar across additional SKUs before production planning locks in for new product launches and trade show commitments.

personalization_hooks.hook: GF already successfully manufactures GF 108 Tedlar laminate, proving operational competency with Tedlar converting processes
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead with recognition of their proven Tedlar manufacturing expertise, then position the conversation as scaling existing operational success into new product categories (wall protection, architectural, transit interiors) rather than learning a new material. Frame it as leveraging their existing capability to drive operational efficiency gains through supplier consolidation and process standardization.

personalization_hooks.hook: Recent co-exhibition with DuPont Tedlar at ISA 2025 with joint anti-graffiti product demonstrations indicates active strategic partnership at executive level
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference the recent ISA collaboration as proof of strong partnership momentum, then transition to discussing how to translate marketing alignment into operational scale. Position the outreach as a natural next step after successful joint trade show activity: moving from co-marketing one SKU (GF 108) to operational planning for expanding Tedlar across multiple product lines.

personalization_hooks.hook: GF launched new Economy Film & Laminate Solutions and GF 767 Sparkle Holographic Film, signaling active product portfolio expansion and manufacturing capacity allocation decisions
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Acknowledge their recent product launches and innovation pace, then frame Tedlar expansion as a way to differentiate their growing portfolio. Position the conversation around operational planning: with new SKUs in market and PRINTING United Expo 2025 coming up, now is the time to evaluate which product lines benefit from upgrading to Tedlar-grade performance to command premium positioning and reduce warranty risk as the portfolio scales.

recommended_approach: Lead with operational efficiency and risk mitigation rather than product features. Acknowledge the existing Tedlar partnership and GF 108 success, then frame the conversation as a strategic operations discussion: How can we help you scale what's already working (Tedlar converting expertise) across more of your product portfolio to improve yield, reduce warranty exposure, and drive higher revenue per manufacturing square foot? Position yourself as a partner in their operational planning, not a vendor selling material.
